children: The State Street SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ETF
is carving out a constructive technical setup as crude prices firm and Middle East risk remains elevated.

On the weekly chart, the fund is beginning to take the shape of an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern—a longer-term formation that technicians watch as a potential shift from basing to trend continuation.

XOP recently traded near $194.50, up +0.3% on the session. The move is modest in isolation, but the broader tape is not: the ETF is higher by +54.1% in 2026 and has gained +130.6% over the past five years. Moreover, assets under management stand at just above $4 billion.
The funds portfolio concentrates U.S. exploration, production, and refining names. Leading holdings include PBF Energy
—companies whose earnings remain tightly linked to refining margins and realized oil prices.
That linkage is back in focus. Brent crude

has pushed above $100 a barrel as U.S.-Iran hostilities and related disruptions around key Gulf shipping lanes keep a risk premium in the market. For XOP, higher crude and tighter supply typically support both producers and refiners in the basket.
